culture.title: Read the Silver Ex-Votos at the Capilla del Cristo
culture.description: Look into the tiny 18th-century chapel at the end of Calle del Cristo, built where a man survived a fall off the city wall, and read the silver offerings on its altar.
culture.bonus: Work out which ex-voto is a thank-you for which body part.

culture.title: See What the MAC Has On in Santurce
culture.description: Go to the only museum on the island built purely for post-war art from Puerto Rico, the Caribbean and Latin America, in an old neo-Gothic school.
culture.bonus: Pick the one piece in the building you would actually live with.

culture.title: Trace the Island's Roots at the Museo de las Américas
culture.description: Go into the Ballajá barracks for the permanent rooms on Taíno, African and Spanish Puerto Rico — the clearest explanation of the island in one building.
culture.bonus: Come out able to name three things on the island that are Taíno in origin.

culture.title: Work Through the Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico
culture.description: Give an afternoon to the island's main art museum in Santurce — five centuries of Puerto Rican work in a 1920s hospital building, with a formal garden behind it.
culture.bonus: Find the stained-glass window at the back and sit with it for five minutes.

culture.title: Tour Casa Blanca, the Oldest House in the Americas
culture.description: Walk through the 1521 house built for Ponce de León's family and lived in by his descendants for 250 years, with terraced gardens dropping to the bay.
culture.bonus: Go out into the back gardens and find the view of the bay through the trees.

culture.title: Stand at Ponce de León's Tomb in the Cathedral
culture.description: Step into the second-oldest cathedral in the Americas, begun in 1521, where the conquistador's remains sit in a marble tomb by the nave.
culture.bonus: Find the glass case with the mummified body of a martyr in it.

culture.title: Learn to Dance Bomba with Taller Tambuyé
culture.description: Take a class in Puerto Rico's oldest rhythm, where the dancer leads and the drummer has to follow — then go and watch them play it live.
culture.bonus: Take the solo in front of the drum instead of hiding at the back.

culture.title: Walk the Murals of Santurce es Ley
culture.description: Spend a morning on the streets around Calle Cerra, where a decade of mural festivals has turned a whole barrio into open-air painting four storeys high.
culture.bonus: Find a mural that has been painted over another one and look for the edges.

8ball.title: Let a Público Driver Pick Your Night
8ball.description: Get in a público or a taxi, ask the driver where they would actually go tonight — not where tourists go — and commit to it, wherever it is.
8ball.bonus: Do not pull your phone out to check the place before you walk in.

8ball.title: Chinchorrear Until the Car Runs Out of Road
8ball.description: Do the island's own national sport: drive out of the city and stop at every roadside chinchorro you pass, one drink and one fried thing at each, until you have to turn back.
8ball.bonus: Make it to five stops and remember the name of every single one.

social.title: Drink at a Piñones Chinchorro After Dark
social.description: Stay out east past sunset when the kiosks turn into bars, the speakers come out and the whole thing becomes a party on the sand.
social.bonus: Stay for the last song the loudest kiosk plays.

social.title: Dance Until Close at Tulum in La Placita
social.description: Pick the club on the edge of the Santurce market where the floor does not empty, and stay on it.
social.bonus: Do not leave the dancefloor for a full hour.

social.title: Pay Cash at El Batey
social.description: Push into the scruffiest, best bar in Old San Juan — graffiti to the ceiling, a jukebox older than you, and no card machine.
social.bonus: Add your name to the wall somewhere nobody will find it.

social.title: Take the Rum Tasting Tour at Casa Bacardí
social.description: Ferry across San Juan Bay to the world's largest premium rum distillery and taste through the reserves, including one you can only get on site.
social.bonus: Go across by ferry rather than by car, and drink the Special Reserve.

social.title: Take In Winter-League Baseball at Hiram Bithorn
social.description: Get a ticket to Liga de Béisbol Profesional Roberto Clemente, where big-league prospects play through the winter to a crowd with drums and horns.
social.bonus: Sit in the loudest section rather than the best seats.

social.title: Crawl the Bars of Calle Loíza
social.description: Work east along the strip the city's own twenty-somethings drink on — taprooms, tiny cocktail rooms and late food, no cruise crowd anywhere.
social.bonus: Start at El Tap and let the bar staff tell you where to go next.

social.title: Watch the Cangrejeros at the Coliseo Roberto Clemente
social.description: Get into a Baloncesto Superior Nacional game at Santurce's 12,500-seat barn, where the home side is part-owned by Bad Bunny and the crowd is relentless.
social.bonus: Learn one crowd chant well enough to join in by the second half.

social.title: Drink Island Craft Beer at La Taberna Lúpulo
social.description: Take a stool at the Calle San Sebastián beer bar that put Puerto Rican craft brewing on the map, and stay until two.
social.bonus: Order three island beers you have never heard of and pick a favourite.

social.title: Drink Under the Chandelier at El San Juan Hotel
social.description: Take a seat in the lobby bar beneath a vast 1950s crystal chandelier, where the hotel band plays and the room has not changed its mind since Sinatra.
social.bonus: Dress like the room expects you to.

social.title: See a Show at the Choliseo
social.description: Get into the island's biggest arena for whoever is playing — the room where Puerto Rico's reggaeton and salsa headliners do their hometown nights.
social.bonus: Stay for the encore even if you do not know the song.

social.title: Take La Placita de Santurce on a Thursday Night
social.description: Turn up at a daytime produce market that closes its streets to cars after six and becomes three blocks of open-air block party.
social.bonus: Dance to salsa at one bar and reggaeton at the one next door, same hour.

social.title: Drink Through All Six Rooms of La Factoría
social.description: Work your way through an unmarked warren of connected bars on Calle San Sebastián — cocktails, then wine, then a back room that turns into a dancefloor.
social.bonus: Find all six rooms and have one drink in each.

chill.title: Sit in the Arcades of the Cuartel de Ballajá
chill.description: Find the big empty courtyard of the old Spanish barracks behind El Morro and sit in the shade of its two storeys of arches.
chill.bonus: Work out how many arches run around the whole courtyard.

chill.title: Fly a Kite on the El Morro Esplanade
chill.description: Buy a kite off a vendor and join the hundred other people flying them on the huge green field running up to the fortress.
chill.bonus: Get yours higher than the fort's flagpole.

chill.title: Wander the Jardín Botánico in Río Piedras
chill.description: Walk the orchid house, bamboo avenue and lotus ponds of the university's botanical garden, away from every tourist in the city.
chill.bonus: Find the bamboo tunnel and walk the whole length of it.

chill.title: Watch the Sun Go Down from La Ventana al Mar
chill.description: Take the open lawn between the Condado towers that opens straight onto the Atlantic and watch the sky go over the water.
chill.bonus: Get there early enough to claim the bench right at the railing.

chill.title: Take a Beach Day in Ocean Park
chill.description: Use the beach the city actually uses — wider, windier and more local than Condado, with kitesurfers off the point.
chill.bonus: Walk the full length of the beach and back before you settle down.

chill.title: Give an Afternoon to Condado Beach
chill.description: Take a towel down to the city's own stretch of Atlantic, five minutes from a cocktail and ten from a fortress.
chill.bonus: Stay in the water until the light goes properly golden.

chill.title: Walk the Paseo de la Princesa to the Raíces Fountain
chill.description: Stroll the tree-lined promenade under the city walls out to the bronze fountain of Puerto Rico's three roots, with the bay on your right.
chill.bonus: Buy a piragua off a cart on the way and finish it before you reach the fountain.

chill.title: Hold a Table on Plaza de Armas and Watch the City
chill.description: Take a coffee at the old main square, under the four statues of the seasons, and watch Old San Juan go past for an hour.
chill.bonus: Stay long enough to see the same person walk past twice.

chill.title: Swim the Calm Water at Balneario El Escambrón
chill.description: Use the sheltered city balneario where the reef knocks the surf down and the water sits flat all day.
chill.bonus: Get there before nine and have the whole cove to yourself.

chill.title: Hang a Hammock in the Coconut Groves at Piñones
chill.description: String up between two palms behind the dunes, buy a cold Medalla off a kiosk and do nothing at all for three hours.
chill.bonus: Fall asleep in it and let the surf wake you up.

adventure.title: Find the Taíno Petroglyphs at Cueva del Indio
adventure.description: Walk out over jagged coastal limestone on the north shore to a collapsed sea cave carved with Taíno petroglyphs, with the Atlantic smashing in below.
adventure.bonus: Find a carving of a face and work out which way it is looking.

adventure.title: Slide the Natural Rock Chutes at Las Paylas
adventure.description: Hike up a creek behind Luquillo to a run of smooth granite chutes that work as a natural waterslide into cold mountain pools.
adventure.bonus: Take the top chute first instead of working up to it.

adventure.title: Sail Out to the Sandbars Off Icacos
adventure.description: Take a catamaran from Fajardo to an uninhabited cay with a shallow turquoise sandbar you can stand up in a mile from shore.
adventure.bonus: Swim from the boat to the sandbar rather than taking the dinghy.

adventure.title: Hike the Angelito Trail to the Río Mameyes
adventure.description: Take the short rainforest trail outside El Yunque's main corridor down to a clear river pool with a rope swing and almost no crowd.
adventure.bonus: Get all the way in — the water is colder than it looks.

adventure.title: Swim the Ocean Pool at Mar Chiquita
adventure.description: Drive the north coast to a crescent of limestone where the Atlantic punches through a gap in the rock into a sheltered natural pool.
adventure.bonus: Time it so you are in the pool when a big set comes over the wall.

adventure.title: Paddle the Mangrove Channels of the Piñones Lagoon
adventure.description: Kayak through the tunnels of red mangrove in the Torrecilla lagoon, fifteen minutes from the city and completely silent.
adventure.bonus: Stop paddling in the narrowest channel and listen for two full minutes.

adventure.title: Get Lost in the Tunnels of Castillo San Cristóbal
adventure.description: Work through the largest Spanish fortification in the Americas — dry moats, tunnels and a sentry box with its own ghost story.
adventure.bonus: Find the Garita del Diablo and stand in it alone.

adventure.title: Walk the Paseo del Morro Around to El Morro
adventure.description: Follow the sea-level promenade along the base of the city walls, then climb up into the six levels of the 16th-century fortress at the headland.
adventure.bonus: Find the garita the postcards use and take the photo nobody else is taking.

adventure.title: Kayak the Glowing Water of Laguna Grande
adventure.description: Paddle a mangrove channel out into a bioluminescent lagoon after dark and watch your paddle blade light up blue with every stroke.
adventure.bonus: Put your hand in the water and hold it still until it stops glowing.

adventure.title: Surf the Break at La Pared in Luquillo
adventure.description: Paddle out at the beach break that Puerto Rico's surf scene actually uses, forty-five minutes east with El Yunque standing behind you.
adventure.bonus: Ride one all the way in to the sand without falling.

adventure.title: Take the Ferry Out to Flamenco Beach on Culebra
adventure.description: Cross to a small island off the east coast for a mile of white sand, a rusting WWII tank in the shallows and water the colour of a swimming pool.
adventure.bonus: Walk past the tank to the far end of the beach where almost nobody goes.

adventure.title: Fly The Beast at Toro Verde
adventure.description: Ride one of the world's longest single-run ziplines head-first across a mountain valley in the central cordillera at up to sixty miles an hour.
adventure.bonus: Go superman-style, face down, and keep your eyes open the whole way.

adventure.title: Paddleboard the Condado Lagoon Hunting Manatees
adventure.description: Take a board out across a protected marine reserve in the middle of the city, where West Indian manatees graze the shallows.
adventure.bonus: Stay out and drifting until a manatee surfaces near you.

adventure.title: Climb to Yokahú Tower and Mount Britton in El Yunque
adventure.description: Drive up into the only tropical rainforest in the US forest system and climb two stone towers above the canopy for a view out to the Atlantic.
adventure.bonus: Get to the top of Mount Britton while the cloud is still sitting on it.

adventure.title: Snorkel the Reef at Escambrón Marine Park
adventure.description: Swim straight off a city beach into a protected reef with parrotfish, eagle rays, hawksbill turtles and the odd manatee in the seagrass.
adventure.bonus: Stay out long enough to find a turtle.

adventure.title: Ride the Paseo Piñones Boardwalk by Bike
adventure.description: Rent a bike and ride the wooden boardwalk and sand track through the coconut groves east of the airport, with the Atlantic on one side the whole way.
adventure.bonus: Stop at whichever kiosk has the longest queue and eat there.

foodie.title: Eat Criollo Cooking at Vianda in Santurce
foodie.description: Take a table at the small Santurce room that cooks Puerto Rican ingredients with a fine-dining hand — start with the calamari and the bacalao.
foodie.bonus: Let them send out whatever the kitchen is excited about that night.

foodie.title: Have Dinner at Santaella in La Placita
foodie.description: Eat José Santaella's Puerto Rican nouvelle cooking in a brick room with an indoor garden, right on the edge of the Santurce market.
foodie.bonus: Eat here first and then walk straight out into La Placita.

foodie.title: Take Coffee in the Ballajá Courtyard at Café Don Ruiz
foodie.description: Drink coffee from a Yauco growing family in the arcaded courtyard of a 19th-century Spanish barracks, with nobody hurrying you.
foodie.bonus: Sit in the courtyard rather than taking it away, and stay an hour.

foodie.title: Work Through Seven Alcapurrias at La Alcapurria Quemá
foodie.description: Order across the whole board at the Santurce walk-up that makes seven different kinds of alcapurria, and eat them standing up.
foodie.bonus: Try the one filling you have never heard of.

foodie.title: Eat a Brunch Made Entirely of Chocolate at Chocobar Cortés
foodie.description: Order chocolate into everything — grilled cheese, burgers, coffee — at the bean-to-bar café run by the family who have made Puerto Rico's chocolate since 1929.
foodie.bonus: Order the one savoury dish with chocolate in it that sounds worst.

foodie.title: Drink a Piña Colada Where It Was Invented
foodie.description: Order the drink at the Caribe Hilton bar that claims to have mixed the first one in 1954, and judge the claim for yourself.
foodie.bonus: Order a second one somewhere else the same night and pick a winner.

foodie.title: Order a Quesito and Café con Leche at Kasalta
foodie.description: Join the queue at the Ocean Park bakery counter for a quesito, a Cubano and the strongest café con leche in the neighbourhood.
foodie.bonus: Order entirely by pointing at the case.

foodie.title: Drink Hill-Grown Island Coffee at Cuatro Sombras
foodie.description: Have a single-estate Puerto Rican coffee at the Old San Juan café run by a family who have farmed the same Yauco hillside since 1846.
foodie.bonus: Take it out to the interior patio instead of the street.

foodie.title: Eat Your Way Down the Luquillo Kiosks
foodie.description: Work along a strip of about sixty beachfront kiosks east of the city — fried seafood, Peruvian, Argentine, cocktails, live salsa at the weekend.
foodie.bonus: Eat something at three different kiosks and rank them before you leave.

foodie.title: Eat Lechón Off the Block on the Pork Highway
foodie.description: Drive up into Guavate on a Sunday, pick a lechonera off the roadside and eat whole spit-roasted pork hacked onto a tray with arroz con gandules.
foodie.bonus: Ask for the crackling straight off the pig, before it goes on the tray.

foodie.title: Eat Fritters on the Sand at Piñones
foodie.description: Pull up at the open-air kiosks in the coconut groves and order bacalaitos, alcapurrias and a cold Medalla with your feet in the sand.
foodie.bonus: Eat a whole bacalaito the size of a dinner plate without putting it down.

foodie.title: Take the Tasting Menu at Marmalade
foodie.description: Sit in the long white room on Calle Fortaleza for a tasting menu of California-French cooking built on Puerto Rican farm produce, with the wine flight.
foodie.bonus: Order the white bean soup even if it is not on your menu.
